ud4.4:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha, in Bamboo Wood, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
ud4.4:1.3: Then at that time venerable Sāriputta and venerable Mahāmoggallāna were living at the Pigeon Vale.
ud4.4:1.4: Then at that time venerable Sāriputta, on a moonlight night, with his hair freshly shaved off, was sitting in the open air, having attained a certain concentration.
ud4.4:2.1: Then at that time two yakkha friends were going from the Northern region to the Southern region, with some business or other.
ud4.4:2.2: Those yakkhas saw venerable Sāriputta, on (that) moonlight night, with his hair freshly shaved off, sat in the open air.
ud4.4:2.3: And after seeing (him), one of those yakkhas said this to the second yakkha:
ud4.4:2.4: “It occurs to me, friend, to give a blow on this ascetic’s head.”
ud4.4:2.5: When that was said, that yakkha said this to the (other) yakkha:
ud4.4:2.7: Eminent is the ascetic, friend, of great power, of great majesty.”
ud4.4:3.1: For a second time that yakkha said this to the (other) yakkha:
ud4.4:3.2: “It occurs to me, friend, to give a blow on this ascetic’s head.”
ud4.4:3.3: For a second time that yakkha said this to the (other) yakkha:
ud4.4:3.5: Eminent is the ascetic, friend, of great power, of great majesty.”
ud4.4:3.6: For a third time that yakkha said this to the (other) yakkha:
ud4.4:3.7: “It occurs to me, friend, to give a blow on this ascetic’s head.”
ud4.4:3.8: For a third time that yakkha said this to the (other) yakkha:
ud4.4:3.10: Eminent is the ascetic, friend, of great power, of great majesty.”
ud4.4:4.1: Then the yakkha taking no notice of that (other) yakkha, gave a blow on the elder venerable Sāriputta’s head:
ud4.4:4.2: it was such a great blow that with that blow a seven, or seven and a half cubit Nāga (elephant) might have been felled, or a great mountain top might have been burst open.
ud4.4:4.3: Then that yakkha (calling out): “I'm burning, I'm burning” right there (and then) fell into the Great Hell.
ud4.4:5.1: Venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw with his divine-eye, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that yakkha giving a blow on venerable Sāriputta’s head. And after seeing (it),
ud4.4:5.2: he went to venerable Sāriputtā, and after going, he said this to venerable Sāriputta:
ud4.4:5.3: “Can you bear up, venerable friend? Can you carry on? Do you have any pain?”
ud4.4:5.4: “I can bear up, friend Moggallāna; I can carry on, friend Moggallāna,
ud4.4:5.5: but I have a little pain on my head.”
ud4.4:6.2: such is the venerable Sāriputta’s great power and great majesty.
ud4.4:6.3: Here, friend Sāriputta, a certain yakkha gave a blow on your head:
ud4.4:6.4: it was such a great blow, that with that blow a seven, or seven and a half cubit Nāga (elephant) might have been felled, or a great mountain top might have been burst open. But then venerable Sāriputta said this:
ud4.4:6.5: ‘I can bear up, friend Moggallāna; I can carry on, friend Moggallāna,
ud4.4:6.6: but I have a little pain on my head.’”
ud4.4:7.2: such is the venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s great power and great majesty, in as much as he can even see a yakkha,
ud4.4:7.3: whereas we at present do not even see a mud-demon!”
ud4.4:8.1: The Fortunate One heard with his divine ear-element, which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, the fitting talk and conversation of these two Great Nāgas.
ud4.4:9.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud4.4:10.1: “For he whose mind is like a rock, ~ steady, and not wavering,
ud4.4:10.4: ~ not agitated by what is agitating,
ud4.4:10.5: For he whose mind is developed thus ~ from where will pain come upon him?”
